text:
sara_customer: Hey team — we've got a customer on prod hitting our embeddings endpoint with a bunch of failing requests since ~08:40 UTC. They say some requests return a dimension mismatch error, and others succeed but with 3-5s latency spikes. Also billing shows a sudden jump in tokens billed. Can someone help triage?

alex_support: Sorry you're seeing this, @sara_customer — can you paste an example request body + response error (redact PII/API keys)? Quick question: are they using the same model name for all calls?

sara_customer: Yep they say they're calling rwd-embed-large but some of the responses claim 1024 dims while our client expects 1536. Example error: `embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024`. Here's a minimal repro they sent (sanitized):

```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-large",
  "input": ["doc1 text", "doc2 text"],
  "batch_size": 64
}
```

And the response for one failing request:

```json
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024",
  "request_id": "req_01Gx..."
}
```

alex_support: Thanks — two fast checks: 1) confirm client library/version and whether it sets any explicit model aliases (some older SDKs map model names); 2) ask them to include the `X-Request-ID` or `X-Trace-ID` header if possible so we can correlate in logs.

sara_customer: Client is a python service using `redwood-sdk==0.9.2`. They claim they always pass model string `rwd-embed-large`. They just captured a trace id `req_01Gx...` from the error.

alex_support: Pasting steps for correlation and quick observability checks: 1) Run a single-request curl to reproduce and include header `X-Trace-ID: my-debug-123`. Example: 

```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Trace-ID: my-debug-123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-large","input":["test doc"]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```

2) In Console -> Traces, search for `my-debug-123` or the `request_id` to see per-request latency spans (network, routing, model-infer, postprocess). 3) Ask them to disable client-side batching (set batch_size=1) to see if dimension mismatch is tied to our server-side batch-assembler.

josh_ml: tagging in — quick notes from the runtime side: embedding dims are fixed per model. rwd-embed-large should return 1536 always. A 1024 vector suggests either the request routed to a different model (e.g., rwd-embed-medium) or postprocess step truncated/converted incorrectly. Two plausible causes we saw before: 1) model alias mapping in older SDKs (alex mentioned) and 2) a regressed deserialization path in the batching layer when payloads cross a size boundary.

josh_ml: To help us rule out routing, can you share the raw response body (hex/base64 if necessary) and the full `x-routing-model` or `x-served-model` headers from the failing response? Our logs record which model binary served the request.

sara_customer: They've provided a failing raw response and the headers: `x-served-model: rwd-embed-medium@v2` and `x-request-id: req_01Gx...`. So it seems the request got routed to medium. But the client insisted they asked for rwd-embed-large.

alex_support: That's the smoking gun — routing fell back to `rwd-embed-medium`. We need to know why. Josh, could a fallback policy cause silent downgrade when capacity is low? If so, why didn't we surface a deprecation/warning in the response?

josh_ml: We do have fallback policies, but they should add a `x-fallback-reason` header when applied (e.g., `capacity_unavailable`). If that header isn't present, two possibilities: 1) a new router codepath didn't set the header on non-streaming embedding calls, or 2) there was a cached alias mapping pointing large -> medium for that customer (legacy override). I'll check router logs for `req_01Gx...` and post back. Meanwhile, please ask the customer to: 1) run the curl with `X-Trace-ID`, 2) turn off batching, 3) confirm SDK mapping with `redwood.SdkClient.get_model_aliases()` (python snippet).

sara_customer: They ran the single curl with `X-Trace-ID: trace-987` and posted the Console trace link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-987 (shared privately). Observability bot shows spans: network 30ms, router 1200ms, infer 80ms, postprocess 10ms. Router span is huge.

observability_bot: Note: Per-request latency breakdown available in Console under Traces -> span `router.lookup` shows 1200ms and `router.fallback_check` shows 1180ms. Logs indicate repeated retries to `rwd-embed-large` due to transient capacity errors. Final served model: `rwd-embed-medium@v2`.

alex_support: Ok that aligns — router retried for capacity then fell back. That would explain both dimension mismatch (served medium) and latency spikes (retries). The billing jump could be because retries are billed for each attempt in our system; we should confirm invoice behavior.

josh_ml: Action items I'm running: 1) search router logs for `req_01Gx...` and any recent code changes to fallback header behavior; 2) verify whether retries increment billing metric (I think yes for attempts that reached model). If the customer hit retries because of transient capacity, they may have been billed multiple times.

alex_support: For the customer: immediate mitigations we can suggest: 
- Pin model to avoid fallback: include `?strict=true` or header `X-Redwood-Strict-Model: true` in calls (example below). This causes requests to fail fast instead of falling back.
- Reduce concurrent batch size or set `batch_size=1` to avoid hitting capacity spikes.
- If they need capacity guarantees, escalate to Dedicated reservations — I can create a ticket for sales/solutions.

```http
POST /v1/embeddings?strict=true
Header: X-Redwood-Strict-Model: true
Body: {"model":"rwd-embed-large","input":["..."]}
```

sara_customer: Thanks — customer wants us to investigate billing for retries, and they'd like a quick patch to ensure they don't silently get downgraded. They're going to test `?strict=true` now.

alex_support: Perfect. If they see `400 Model not available (strict mode)` that's expected — we'll add visibility in responses for non-strict mode going forward. Josh, can you follow up with a small router patch to ensure `x-fallback-reason` is always set when fallback happens and include the served model in the response headers? That will help debugging.

josh_ml: Yep — I'll open an infra PR to enforce setting those headers and add a short-term metric on fallback counts per tenant. I'll post PR link and ETA in this thread.

sara_customer: Update: customer flipped `strict=true` and now gets `503 Model not available (strict mode)` — they prefer failing fast. Also confirmed billing team flagged 3 attempts for the window that match router retries. They're ok with us refunding the extra attempts if we honor they retried due to our transient capacity.

alex_support: Thanks — I'll open a billing case referencing `req_01Gx...` and `req_01Gy...` (three attempts). We'll request pro-rated credit for the extra attempts due to system retries.

josh_ml: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/router/pull/432 — adds `x-fallback-reason` and `x-served-model` on all embedding responses and increments a fallback telemetry metric. ETA: 2 business days for rollout.

alex_support: Great. Closing loop here: 1) root cause: router retry -> fallback to smaller model due to capacity -> caused dim mismatch and billing for retries. 2) Short-term: customer can set strict=true to fail fast and avoid silent downgrade. 3) Medium-term: router change to surface headers + billing case for refund. 4) Long-term: recommend Dedicated capacity if they need stability for high-throughput embedding workloads.

sara_customer: Customer accepted the plan and appreciated the quick triage. Thanks all :thumbsup:

observability_bot: Note: Ticket `SUP-6421` created for billing refund request and `INFRA-987` created for router header fix.

alex_support: I'll keep this thread updated. If anyone else sees similar reports, please reference `SUP-6421`.
